## I3
One-Sentence Story: Remembering an unsuccessful search requires remembering what was observable.
Theme: World Models - Architecture
Direction Axis: memory-representation
Target Failure: stale-or-conflicting-memory
Direction Evidence: An occluded search and an exhaustive search imply different future actions.
Form: new problem
Summary: Store searched visibility regions alongside negative findings.
Minimal Falsification Experiment: Generate 2,000 simulated cabinet-search episodes; use 1 A100-day. Compare visibility-tagged negative memory against validation-best object-belief and recurrent baselines at equal tokens and training. Test 200 paired episodes under each of full and partial visibility. Primary metric: objects recovered within 30 actions/200. Expect ≥10-point improvement under occlusion. Kill claim if visibility-tag permutation changes success <5 points; kill representation if gain ≤0. Match object locations and camera trajectories.
Why It May Be Novel: Investigate the action consequences of remembering evidence coverage rather than absence alone.
story: Remembering an unsuccessful search requires remembering what was observable.
